about.ex: The trip takes about two hours.

accepted.en: agreed that something is fair or right
accepted.ex: She accepted the job offer last week.

accepting.en: agreeing that something is fair or right
accepting.ex: Accepting help is sometimes hard for proud people.

accepts.en: agrees that something is fair or right
accepts.ex: He accepts that he made a mistake.

accommodate.en: to have enough space or capacity for
accommodate.ex: The new school can accommodate 600 students.

accounts.en: records of money spent and received
accounts.ex: The accounts show the firm made a profit.
accounts.zh: Public Accounts Committee：公共帳目委員會；帳目

acknowledge.en: to admit that something is true
acknowledge.ex: He refused to acknowledge his mistake.

acquisition.en: the act of getting or buying something
acquisition.ex: The acquisition of new land took two years.

across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

address.ex: The council must address the housing shortage.

advance.en: in advance of: before; ahead of
advance.ex: Please book your tickets well in advance.

advocating.ex: The group is advocating cleaner public transport.

example.en: Many experts advocate using less water at home.
example.zh: 許多專家提倡在家中少用水。

note.meaning: 提倡；公開主張或支持某做法。
note.usage: advocate 後直接接名詞或動名詞（不加 for）；名詞 advocate 指「倡導者」，如 an advocate of reform。

noteEn.meaning: to publicly support or recommend something.
noteEn.usage: As a verb, it takes a noun or -ing form directly, without 'for'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Muchos expertos abogan por usar menos agua en casa.
noteEs.usage: Como verbo va seguido directamente de sustantivo o forma -ing (sin for).

noteHi.exampleTr: कई विशेषज्ञ घर में कम पानी इस्तेमाल करने की वकालत करते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी विचार का सार्वजनिक रूप से समर्थन करना।
noteHi.usage: क्रिया के बाद सीधे संज्ञा या -ing रूप आता है (for नहीं)।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの専門家が家庭での節水を提唱している。
noteJa.meaning: ある考えや方法を公に支持・推奨する。
noteJa.usage: 動詞の後に直接名詞か動名詞を置く（for は不要）。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 전문가들이 가정에서 물을 덜 쓰자고 주장한다.
noteKo.usage: 동사 뒤에 바로 명사나 동명사가 온다(for 없이).

ageing.en: becoming old and in worse condition
ageing.ex: The town's ageing bridges need urgent repairs.

all-time.en: the highest or lowest ever recorded
all-time.ex: Sales hit an all-time high this year.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

ambitions.en: big goals or plans someone wants to achieve
ambitions.ex: Her ambitions include running her own company.

among.zh: chief among：其中最主要的；在…之中

annually.ex: The festival is held annually in May.

answer.ex: Please answer all the questions on the form.

anticipated.ja: 見込まれる；期待される

any.en: one of many, no matter which

appear.en: to come before an official group to answer questions
appear.ex: The minister will appear before the court next week.

approval.ex: The plan still needs approval from the council.

approximately.ex: The flight takes approximately three hours.

area.en: a part of a city or country
area.ex: This area has many good restaurants.

argues.en: says something is true and gives reasons
argues.ex: She argues that taxes should be lower.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the party.

as.zh: 作為；（billed as：被稱為；such as：例如）

assets.en: useful things a company owns, like pipes and plants
assets.ex: The company sold some assets to pay its debts.

at.en: shows a place, time or level

away.en: from someone, so they no longer have it
away.ex: Please take these old boxes away.

back.ex: The meeting was pushed back to Friday.

bad.ex: I'm afraid I have some bad news.

benefits.ex: Regular exercise has many health benefits.

better.ex: The new phone is much better than the old one.

big.ex: They live in a big house near the sea.

billed.ex: The match was billed as the game of the year.

billing.en: sending bills to customers for payment
billing.ex: Billing errors made many customers angry.

bolster.ex: Good results bolster the team's confidence.

boss.ex: My boss let me leave early today.

bottleneck.en: a point where things get stuck and slow down
bottleneck.ex: The narrow bridge creates a bottleneck every morning.

example.en: Slow planning approval is the main bottleneck in housing.
example.zh: 規劃審批緩慢是住房建設的主要瓶頸。

note.meaning: 瓶頸；使整個流程變慢或受阻的環節。
note.usage: 可指交通或流程，常用 a bottleneck in sth；也可說 create/cause a bottleneck。

noteEn.meaning: a point that slows down a whole process.
noteEn.usage: Often 'a bottleneck in something' or 'create/cause a bottleneck'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La lentitud de los permisos es el principal cuello de botella en la vivienda.
noteEs.meaning: punto donde todo el proceso se atasca o se ralentiza.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a bottleneck in algo; también create/cause a bottleneck.

noteHi.exampleTr: धीमी योजना मंज़ूरी आवास निर्माण की मुख्य अड़चन है।
noteHi.meaning: वह बिंदु जहाँ पूरी प्रक्रिया धीमी या रुक जाती है।
noteHi.usage: a bottleneck in sth; create/cause a bottleneck भी आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 遅い計画承認が住宅建設の主なボトルネックだ。
noteJa.meaning: 全体の流れを遅らせたり止めたりする箇所。
noteJa.usage: a bottleneck in ～ や create/cause a bottleneck の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 느린 계획 승인이 주택 건설의 주요 병목이다.
noteKo.meaning: 전체 과정을 느리게 하거나 막는 지점.
noteKo.usage: a bottleneck in ~, create/cause a bottleneck 형태로 자주 쓴다.

briefing.ex: The minister received a briefing on the crisis.

bring.en: to move something to a place
bring.ex: Can you bring some water to the table?

bringing.ex: Bringing the old house up to date was expensive.

building.en: the work of making houses, pipes, etc.

business.en: trade; business case: reasons a project is worthwhile
business.ex: She wrote a business case for the new office.
business.ja: ビジネス（business case：事業計画の根拠）
business.zh: business case：商業論證（可行性論證）；商業

businesses.en: companies that sell goods or services
businesses.ex: Many local businesses closed during the storm.

buying.ex: Buying a home is a big decision.

by.en: shows who does something or how much

calling.ex: Doctors are calling for a ban on smoking in cars.

capacity.en: the amount something can hold or supply
capacity.ex: The stadium has a capacity of 50,000 people.

capital.en: the main city of a country
capital.ex: Paris is the capital of France.

carry.en: to have something as a feature or cost
carry.ex: The job carries a lot of responsibility.
carry.zh: carry a price tag：需要花費（附帶…價格）

case.en: a set of reasons for doing something
case.ex: She made a strong case for hiring more staff.
case.zh: business case：商業論證（可行性論證）

cautions.ex: The doctor cautions against eating too much salt.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent last year.

central.ex: Education is central to the government's plans.

century.en: a period of one hundred years
century.ex: The church was built in the 12th century.
century.zh: 世紀（a quarter of a century：二十五年）

certain.ex: We need a more certain timetable for the work.

certainty.en: being sure about what will happen
certainty.ex: Investors want certainty before they spend money.

channel.en: to send water or something along a route
channel.ex: Farmers channel river water to their fields.

chief.ex: Cost was the chief reason for the delay.
chief.zh: 首席的；主要的（chief executive：執行長）

clean.en: to make water free of dirt
clean.ex: This filter cleans the water you drink.

clearer.ex: The new rules are much clearer than the old ones.

comfortable.ex: The interview was not very comfortable for him.

commission.en: an official group with special powers
commission.ex: A commission was set up to investigate the accident.
commission.zh: 委員會（Commission for Regulation of Utilities：公用事業監管委員會）

commissioning.en: testing a new system and starting to use it
commissioning.ex: Commissioning of the new power plant took six months.

committee.en: a group chosen to discuss and decide things

communities.en: groups of people living in one area
communities.ex: Rural communities often lack good internet.

company.ex: He works for a software company.

compliance.ex: Factories must show compliance with safety laws.

example.en: All new buildings must be in compliance with safety rules.
example.zh: 所有新建築都必須符合安全規定。

note.meaning: 合規；遵守法律、規定或標準。
note.usage: 常用 compliance with sth；regulatory compliance 指符合監管要求。動詞為 comply with。

noteEn.usage: Use 'compliance with something'; the verb is 'comply with'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Todos los edificios nuevos deben cumplir las normas de seguridad.
noteEs.meaning: el hecho de cumplir leyes, normas o estándares.
noteEs.usage: Se usa compliance with algo; el verbo es comply with.

noteHi.exampleTr: सभी नई इमारतों को सुरक्षा नियमों का पालन करना होगा।
noteHi.meaning: नियमों या मानकों का पालन करना।
noteHi.usage: compliance with sth आम है; क्रिया comply with है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい建物はすべて安全規則に適合していなければならない。
noteJa.meaning: 法律・規則・基準を守ること。
noteJa.usage: compliance with ～ の形。動詞は comply with。

noteKo.exampleTr: 모든 신축 건물은 안전 규정을 준수해야 한다.
noteKo.usage: compliance with ~ 형태로 쓰며 동사는 comply with이다.

comprehensive.ex: The report gives a comprehensive review of the problem.

concede.en: to admit something is true, often unwillingly
concede.ex: The coach conceded that his team played badly.

consent.ex: You need written consent to build an extension.
consent.zh: 許可；同意（environmental consent：環境許可）

consenting.ex: The new consenting process is faster for builders.

consents.ex: The developer obtained all the necessary consents.

consequently.ex: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.

example.en: The pipes were old; consequently, many leaks appeared.
example.zh: 水管老舊，因此出現許多漏水。

note.meaning: 因此；結果。用來引出前述情況所造成的結果。
note.usage: 常放句首並加逗號，正式程度高於 so；與 as a result 同義。

noteEn.meaning: as a result of what was just said.
noteEn.usage: Often at the start of a sentence with a comma; more formal than 'so'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las tuberías eran viejas; por consiguiente, aparecieron muchas fugas.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio de la oración con coma; es más formal que so.

noteHi.exampleTr: पाइप पुराने थे; परिणामस्वरूप कई रिसाव हुए।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर वाक्य की शुरुआत में अल्पविराम के साथ; so से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 管が古かったため、その結果多くの漏水が起きた。
noteJa.meaning: その結果として。前の内容から生じる結果を示す。
noteJa.usage: 文頭にコンマと共に置くことが多く、so より硬い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 관이 낡아서 그 결과 누수가 많이 생겼다.
noteKo.meaning: 그 결과로. 앞의 상황 때문에 생긴 결과를 나타낸다.
noteKo.usage: 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 자주 쓰이며 so보다 격식 있다.

considerably.ex: Prices have risen considerably this year.

construction.ex: Construction of the bridge will take two years.

contained.ex: The details are contained in this letter.

contends.en: argues or claims that something is true
contends.ex: He contends that the test was unfair.

contingent.ex: Our trip is contingent on the weather.

example.en: The new bridge is contingent on government funding.
example.zh: 新橋能否興建取決於政府撥款。

note.meaning: 取決於；視…而定。表示某事能否發生要看另一件事。
note.usage: 常用 be contingent on/upon sth，多見於正式書面語；upon 比 on 更正式。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'be contingent on/upon something'; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: El nuevo puente está supeditado a la financiación del gobierno.
noteEs.meaning: que depende de que ocurra otra cosa.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be contingent on/upon algo, sobre todo en registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: नया पुल सरकारी धन पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी दूसरी बात पर निर्भर होना।
noteHi.usage: be contingent on/upon sth औपचारिक लेखन में प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しい橋は政府の資金次第だ。
noteJa.meaning: 他の事柄次第で決まる、条件付きである。
noteJa.usage: be contingent on/upon ～ の形で、主に硬い書き言葉で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 다리는 정부 자금 지원에 달려 있다.
noteKo.usage: be contingent on/upon ~ 형태로 주로 격식 있는 글에서 쓴다.

cost.en: to need a certain amount of money

costs.ex: Rising energy costs worry many families.

country.en: a nation with its own land and government
country.ex: Canada is a very large country.

country's.ex: The country's economy is growing slowly.

creaking.ex: The country's creaking railways need investment.
creaking.ja: 老朽化してガタがきた
creaking.zh: 老舊不堪的；運作吃力的

create.ex: The factory will create 200 new jobs.

crews.ex: Repair crews worked through the night.

cut.ex: The shop cut its prices for the sale.

deal.ex: She deals with complaints every day.

decision.en: a choice or ruling that has been made

declined.ex: Car sales have declined this year.

deficiencies.en: faults or things that are lacking
deficiencies.ex: The report found serious deficiencies in the system.

delay.en: a time when something happens later than planned
delay.ex: There was a long delay at the airport.

delivery.ex: The project's delivery was ahead of schedule.

describes.ex: She describes her job as stressful.

deteriorating.ex: The deteriorating roads are dangerous for cyclists.

example.en: Engineers warned about the deteriorating state of the bridge.
example.zh: 工程師就這座橋日益惡化的狀況發出警告。

note.meaning: 日益惡化的；逐漸變差、老化的。
note.usage: 來自動詞 deteriorate（惡化），常修飾 conditions、health、infrastructure 等。

noteEn.usage: From the verb 'deteriorate'; used with conditions, health, buildings.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los ingenieros advirtieron sobre el estado de deterioro del puente.
noteEs.meaning: que empeora o se deteriora poco a poco.
noteEs.usage: Viene del verbo deteriorate; acompaña a conditions, health, infrastructure.

noteHi.exampleTr: इंजीनियरों ने पुल की बिगड़ती हालत के बारे में चेतावनी दी।
noteHi.usage: क्रिया deteriorate से बना; conditions, health, infrastructure के साथ आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 技術者たちは橋の劣化しつつある状態について警告した。
noteJa.meaning: 次第に悪化している、劣化しつつある。
noteJa.usage: 動詞 deteriorate から。conditions, health, infrastructure などを修飾する。

noteKo.exampleTr: 기술자들은 다리의 악화되는 상태에 대해 경고했다.
noteKo.usage: 동사 deteriorate에서 나왔으며 conditions, health, infrastructure 등을 꾸민다.

disrupt.ex: The strike will disrupt train services.
disrupt.ja: 混乱させる；支障をきたす

disruption.en: problems that stop normal life or work
disruption.ex: The roadworks caused disruption for weeks.

dividends.ex: Hard work in school pays dividends later.

docked.en: took away money as a punishment
docked.ex: His pay was docked for arriving late.

document.ex: Please sign the document at the bottom.

drainage.en: a system that takes away dirty or extra water
drainage.ex: Poor drainage causes flooding in the streets.

drive.en: drive up: make prices or costs higher
drive.ex: High demand can drive up house prices.

due.ex: The train is due to arrive at six.

dáil.en: the lower house of Ireland's parliament
dáil.hi: डाइल (आयरलैंड की संसद का निचला सदन)
dáil.ja: ドイル（アイルランド下院）

dáil's.en: belonging to Ireland's lower house of parliament

economic.en: relating to trade, industry and money
economic.ex: The country has seen strong economic growth.

efficiency.en: working well without wasting time or money
efficiency.ex: New machines improved the factory's efficiency.

efficient.ex: Trains are an efficient way to travel.

encompassing.ex: The course encompasses history, art and music.

energy.en: power such as electricity and gas

enhance.ex: Good lighting can enhance a room.

enterprise.ex: The town wants to attract more enterprise.

entirely.ex: I'm not entirely sure what she meant.

environmental.en: about nature and the natural world
environmental.ex: Plastic waste is a serious environmental problem.

equivalent.ex: One mile is equivalent to about 1.6 kilometres.

estimate.en: a guess of a number or cost
estimate.ex: The builder gave us an estimate for the repairs.

estimated.en: guessed the size or cost of
estimated.ex: Experts estimated the damage at €2 million.

eventually.en: in the end; after a long time
eventually.ex: We eventually found the right house.

ever.ex: This is the best meal I have ever eaten.
ever.ja: かつて（than ever：これまでになく）
ever.zh: 曾經（lower than ever：前所未有地低）

evidence.en: information given to an official group
evidence.ex: Three witnesses gave evidence in court.

executive.en: a senior manager of a company

expansion.ex: The airport's expansion will create many jobs.

expected.ex: Prices are expected to rise next year.

expenditure.ex: Public expenditure on health has increased.

expensive.ex: That restaurant is too expensive for me.

explained.ex: The teacher explained the rules clearly.

face.ex: The manager will face tough questions tomorrow.

failing.ex: He was fined for failing to pay his taxes.

fallen.ex: The number of visitors has fallen sharply.

falling.en: falling short of: not reaching a target
falling.ex: The team is falling short of its sales goal.

faster.ex: The new train is faster than the old one.

felt.ex: The effects of the storm were felt for days.

figure.ex: The official figure is lower than expected.

figures.ex: The latest figures show unemployment is falling.

financial.ex: The club is having financial problems.

five-year.ex: The government announced a five-year plan.

fix.ex: Can you fix my bike this weekend?

fixing.ex: He spent the day fixing the roof.

flagship.ex: The store is the brand's flagship shop in London.

for.en: used to show purpose or who gets something

from.en: starting at a place or point

furthermore.ex: The house is cheap; furthermore, it is near the station.

future.ex: Nobody knows what the future will bring.

gauntlet.en: a long series of difficult tests or problems
gauntlet.ex: New drugs must run a gauntlet of safety tests.

getting.ex: Getting a visa can take months.

give.ex: She will give a talk about climate change.

gleeson.en: surname of Uisce Éireann's chief executive

go.ex: All new laws go through several stages.

greater.en: more; also used for a city and its wider area
greater.ex: We need greater support from the government.
greater.zh: 更大的（Greater Dublin：大都柏林地區）

group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

growth.en: an increase in size or amount
growth.ex: The city has seen rapid population growth.

having.en: form of 'have' used before a past participle
having.zh: 已經（having dropped：在下降了之後）

hearing.en: an official meeting where people answer questions
hearing.ex: The court hearing lasted three hours.

help.ex: This app helps you learn new words.

historical.ex: The city is tackling historical problems with traffic.

hold-up.ex: Sorry, there was a hold-up at the bank.

homes.en: houses or flats where people live
homes.ex: The builders plan 300 new homes here.

housing.en: houses and flats for people to live in
housing.ex: Young people struggle to find affordable housing.

if.en: used to talk about a condition

importance.ex: Never underestimate the importance of sleep.

imposed.en: officially put on someone as a rule or penalty
imposed.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.

improve.ex: I want to improve my English.

improvement.en: a change that makes something better
improvement.ex: There has been a big improvement in her health.

improvements.ex: The school made several improvements this year.

including.en: with something as part of a group

income.ex: Tourism is the island's main source of income.

inconvenience.en: to cause problems or trouble for
inconvenience.ex: I hope our visit won't inconvenience you.

incurred.en: had something bad happen as a result of actions
incurred.ex: The firm incurred heavy losses last year.

indispensable.en: so important you cannot manage without it
indispensable.ex: A good dictionary is indispensable for students.

example.en: A reliable water supply is indispensable to a modern city.
example.zh: 可靠的供水對現代城市來說不可或缺。

note.meaning: 不可或缺的；絕對必要的。語氣比 essential 更強。
note.usage: 常用 be indispensable to/for sth；多用於正式或學術寫作。

noteEn.meaning: so necessary that you cannot manage without it.

noteEs.exampleTr: Un suministro de agua fiable es indispensable para una ciudad moderna.
noteEs.meaning: tan necesario que no se puede prescindir de ello.
noteEs.usage: Se usa be indispensable to/for algo, en estilo formal o académico.

noteHi.exampleTr: आधुनिक शहर के लिए भरोसेमंद जल आपूर्ति अपरिहार्य है।
noteHi.meaning: इतना ज़रूरी कि उसके बिना काम न चले।
noteHi.usage: be indispensable to/for sth औपचारिक लेखन में आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 信頼できる給水は近代都市に不可欠だ。
noteJa.meaning: それなしでは済まないほど必要な。essential より強い。
noteJa.usage: be indispensable to/for ～ の形で、フォーマルな文章でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 안정적인 물 공급은 현대 도시에 필수 불가결하다.
noteKo.meaning: 그것 없이는 안 될 만큼 꼭 필요한.
noteKo.usage: be indispensable to/for ~ 형태로 격식 있는 글에서 자주 쓴다.

inevitably.en: in a way that cannot be avoided
inevitably.ex: Big changes inevitably cause some stress.

example.en: Road repairs inevitably cause some traffic delays.
example.zh: 道路維修不可避免地會造成一些交通延誤。

note.meaning: 不可避免地；必然地。表示某事一定會發生。
note.usage: 常放在動詞前或句首；形容詞為 inevitable，常用 it is inevitable that…。

noteEn.meaning: in a way that cannot be avoided.
noteEn.usage: Usually before the verb or at the start; adjective 'inevitable'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las obras en la carretera causan inevitablemente algunos retrasos.
noteEs.meaning: de un modo que no se puede evitar.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir antes del verbo o al inicio; el adjetivo es inevitable.

paragraphs: Uisce Éireann runs the water system in Ireland. It says it needs a lot of money to make the system better. It needs about €2 billion every year for the next 25 years. That is €50 billion in total.
The company sent this plan to a group of TDs in the Dáil. Its boss, Niall Gleeson, will speak to the group on Thursday.
The money will pay for new pipes and new plants to clean water. One big plan will bring water from the River Shannon to Dublin. Ireland also needs water for many new homes.

There is a problem too. The company did not stop enough leaks in the past. A regulator took €31 million away from it. But the company says leaks are now at their lowest level. In 2014, 49% of water was lost. Now it is 36%.
Uisce Éireann, the company that runs Ireland's water services, says it will cost about €50 billion to improve the country's water system. It needs around €2 billion every year for the next 25 years.
The company explained its plans in a document for the Dáil's Public Accounts Committee. Its chief executive, Niall Gleeson, is due to answer questions from the committee on Thursday.

The money would pay to repair and improve old pipes and treatment plants across the country. It would also help the system deal with problems in the future and make room for new homes and businesses. Two very large projects are planned. One would bring water from the River Shannon to Dublin through a long pipeline. The other is a new drainage system for the Dublin area.

Big projects like these go through many steps, such as planning, buying land, getting permission and building. A delay at one step can make the whole project slower and more expensive. The company wants these steps to be faster and clearer.
Mr Gleeson also plans to warn that building work will cause problems for local people, often a long time before they see the benefits. He says the company will try to keep this to a minimum.

The company has also had bad news. The energy and water regulator cut its income by €31 million because it missed targets on fixing leaks and on billing businesses. Uisce Éireann accepts this, but it says leaks are now lower than ever. In 2014, 49% of the country's water was lost through leaks. Today the figure is 36%, and in the Dublin area it is under 30%. Workers fix about 2,000 leaks every month.
The company says water for new housing is a top priority.

Uisce Éireann, the national water utility, has estimated that upgrading Ireland's water and wastewater networks will cost roughly €50 billion over the next quarter of a century, or about €2 billion a year.
The figures appear in a briefing document prepared for the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, where chief executive Niall Gleeson is expected to face questions on Thursday.

According to the utility, the investment is needed to maintain and modernise ageing infrastructure, tackle long-standing weaknesses, make the system more resilient and create capacity for housing and economic growth. Two major schemes stand out: a project to pipe water from the River Shannon to the capital, and the Greater Dublin Drainage Project. The company describes both as once-in-a-generation projects of national importance.

Large projects must pass through a series of linked stages, including business case approval, planning, land purchase, environmental consents, procurement and construction. Uisce Éireann warns that a hold-up at any stage can raise costs and delay benefits, and it is calling for a more certain and efficient approval process.

Mr Gleeson is also expected to acknowledge that construction will disrupt local communities, sometimes long before any improvements are felt, and to promise that the company will limit unnecessary disruption.

The utility is likely to be questioned about a €31 million penalty imposed by the Commission for Regulation of Utilities after it missed targets on leakage and non-domestic billing over five years. While accepting the decision, the company insists that leakage has fallen to a record low: from 49 per cent in 2014 to 36 per cent nationally, and below 30 per cent in the Greater Dublin Area. Crews repair about 2,000 leaks a month across a network of some 65,000km.

Bringing Ireland's water infrastructure up to standard will carry a price tag of around €50 billion, according to Uisce Éireann, which says it will require roughly €2 billion annually for the next 25 years.
The estimate is set out in a briefing paper submitted to the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, before which the utility's chief executive, Niall Gleeson, is scheduled to appear on Thursday.

The outlay, the company argues, is essential to overhaul a creaking network, address a legacy of underinvestment, bolster resilience and compliance, and unlock capacity for new housing and enterprise. Chief among its ambitions are a scheme to channel water from the River Shannon to Dublin and the Greater Dublin Drainage Project, both billed as once-in-a-generation undertakings.

Such schemes must navigate a gauntlet of interlocking stages, from securing approval for the business case to planning, land acquisition, environmental consents, procurement and, eventually, commissioning. A bottleneck at any point, the utility cautions, can drive up costs and push back the benefits, which is why it is pressing for a more predictable consenting regime.

Mr Gleeson is also poised to concede that construction will inevitably inconvenience local communities, frequently well before the dividends materialise, though he pledges to keep avoidable disruption to a minimum.

The hearing is unlikely to be entirely comfortable. The Commission for Regulation of Utilities recently docked the company €31 million for falling short of targets on leakage and non-domestic billing over a five-year period. Uisce Éireann has accepted the sanction, yet maintains that leakage is at an all-time low, having dropped from 49 per cent in 2014 to 36 per cent nationwide and under 30 per cent in the Greater Dublin Area.

Uisce Éireann has estimated that a comprehensive upgrade of Ireland's water and wastewater systems will necessitate investment of approximately €50 billion, equivalent to some €2 billion per annum over a 25-year period.
This projection is contained in a briefing document submitted to the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, at which the utility's chief executive, Niall Gleeson, is due to give evidence on Thursday.

The utility contends that such substantial expenditure is indispensable if it is to maintain deteriorating assets, remedy historical deficiencies, enhance resilience and regulatory compliance, and provide sufficient capacity to accommodate housing and economic expansion. Two flagship initiatives are central to this strategy: the transfer of water from the River Shannon to the capital and the Greater Dublin Drainage Project.

Nevertheless, the successful delivery of these projects is contingent upon a sequence of interdependent phases, encompassing business case approval, planning permission, land acquisition, environmental consent, procurement and construction. Consequently, a delay at any single phase may significantly inflate costs and postpone the anticipated benefits. The utility is therefore advocating greater certainty and efficiency in the approval process.
